commands.description: Evaluates the expression in `FILE.nix`, or the one `--expr` gives, and prints its value as `nix-instantiate --eval` prints it. A part of the value the evaluation never needed prints as `<CODE>`; with `--strict` the whole value is evaluated first. A relative path resolves against the file's directory, or for `--expr` against the working directory. A `<name>` path is looked up in the entries `--nix-path` adds, then `NIX_PATH`'s, then the `<nix/*>` expressions nova-nix ships with.

examples.description: Print an attribute set as far as evaluating it forced it.
Evaluate the whole value before printing it.
Print the `.drv` a derivation is written to the store as, to compare it with another evaluator's.
Evaluate an expression from a nixpkgs checkout in the working directory.

commands.name: nova-nix eval

commands.description: Evaluates `FILE.nix`, or the expression `--expr` gives, selects the attribute `-A` names when it is given, builds the derivation that results and every derivation it depends on, and prints the path of the output its `outputName` names, the first of its outputs unless the expression selects another, as `nix-build` does. A derivation whose outputs a substituter holds is downloaded instead of built, from the substituters `nix.conf` configures and the one `--substituter` adds, and only a path signed by a trusted key is accepted. A substituter that fails stops the build unless `fallback` is on. With `--out-link` the output is linked from `PATH` and kept from garbage collection; without it nothing is linked, where `nix-build` links `./result`.

examples.description: Build GNU Hello for Windows from the directory a release unpacks to, with the public cache as a substituter.
Build an attribute of a file and link the output from `./result`, a root the garbage collector keeps.

commands.description: Uploads the closure of each `PATH`, or with `--all` every valid path except derivations, to the nova-cache server at `URL`, which signs what it receives. A `PATH` is a store path, in full or as its base name; a derivation is refused, since a binary cache serves outputs. Paths the cache already holds are skipped, every NAR is uploaded before any narinfo announces it, and a narinfo is read back to check that the server signed it. It prints how many paths it pushed and how many the cache already held.

examples.description: Push every path in the store except derivations, compressed with zstd, to a cache that takes the API key in `cache-api-key`.

commands.name: nova-nix push

synopsis.summary: Push store paths (and their closures) to a binary cache
Push every valid path except derivations, and their closures

commands.description: Deletes each `PATH`'s registration and its tree on disk, in the order given, and prints each one it deleted. A `PATH` is a store path, in full or as its base name, and an entry with only a registration or only a tree is deleted too. A path a root keeps, or that another valid path references, is refused, and the first refusal stops the command, so a path is named before the paths it references.

examples.description: Delete a build's output, here GNU Hello's, so that the next build makes it again; `HASH` stands for the hash in its path.

commands.name: nova-nix store delete

synopsis.summary: Remove store paths, refused while a root or another valid path keeps them

commands.description: Deletes every store path no root keeps, directly or through the paths that reference it, and prints how many it deleted and the space it freed, as `nix-store --gc` does. The roots are the out-links `build --out-link` registered and the links and files under the store's `.nova-nix/gcroots` directory; a path a running program has open is not a root, and a rooted output does not keep the `.drv` that built it. With `--print-roots` it lists the roots and deletes nothing.

examples.description: List the roots, each as the link that names it and the path it keeps.

commands.name: nova-nix store gc

synopsis.summary: Remove every store path not reachable from a root

configuration.description: `nix.conf` is read in upstream's order: `$NIX_CONF_DIR/nix.conf`, where `NIX_CONF_DIR` defaults to `/etc/nix`, or `%ProgramData%\nix` on Windows; the XDG `nix/nix.conf` files or `$NIX_USER_CONF_FILES`; then `$NIX_CONFIG`. A later source replaces an earlier one's value, an `extra-` prefix on a list setting adds to it instead, and a flag adds to whatever they configure.

global.description: nova-nix evaluates Nix expressions, builds derivations, pushes store paths to a binary cache and maintains its store, one command per invocation, and reads its settings from `nix.conf` as upstream Nix does. Each command takes the flags listed with it, after the command's name. A command exits with status 0 when it succeeds, and with status 1 when it fails, after saying why on stderr.
